title: One-step effect of an oracle call
statement: Let $A$ be an instruction program on $m$ registers with control states in $\Lambda$, let the oracle answer Boolean queries to $d$ deciders, and fix its initial state $l_0$ and a Boolean input $x$. Suppose the instruction at state $l$ is a call to decider $j$ in mode $\mu$ with argument-register list $R$, branching to $l_1$ on a positive answer and to $l_0'$ on a negative answer. For any register assignment $v$ and output word $o$, one step of the program from the configuration in state $l$, at the start phase, with input head at position one and register tapes storing the binary expansions of $v$, yields the corresponding start-phase configuration with the same registers, input-head position, and output, and state $l_1$ if the oracle accepts the virtual input formed from $x$, mode $\mu$, and the words in registers $R$, or state $l_0'$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: The register program $A$, oracle, and initial state $l_0$
The instruction at $l$ is the specified call
